riess2022.reference: Riess et al. 2022, ApJ 934, L7 (arXiv:2112.04510), 'A Comprehensive Measurement of H0 from SH0ES'
riess2022.where: Section 6.2 (the primary analysis finds a metallicity dependence on [O/H] of -0.217 +- 0.046 mag/dex); equation (1): m_W = mu0 + M_W + b_W (log P - 1) + Z_W [O/H], [O/H] relative to the Sun
riess2022.zRefMeaning: solar, 12 + log(O/H) = 8.69 (Asplund et al. 2009), Table 3 note a
riess2022.band: HST WFC3 Wesenheit magnitude F160W - 0.386 (F555W - F814W)
riess2022.licence: arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the abs page); the paper is open access in ApJL. Used for quoting a few published numbers with credit; nothing is bundled.

breuval2022.reference: Breuval et al. 2022, ApJ 939, 89 (arXiv:2205.06280), 'An Improved Calibration of the Wavelength Dependence of Metallicity on the Cepheid Leavitt Law'
breuval2022.where: Table 4, row W_H (*): gamma = -0.280 +- 0.078 mag/dex (a fit to the Milky Way, LMC and SMC without the HST SMC photometry or the individual metallicities of Riess et al. 2022); its Table 1 lists R22's -0.217 +- 0.046 beside it
breuval2022.licence: arXiv page links CC BY 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); quoting a few numbers with credit

hosts.source: Riess et al. 2022, Table 3 (<[O/H]> by galaxy, dex relative to the Sun) and Section 3.5; the LMC value is the spectroscopic mean of 60 percent of the Cepheids ([O/H] = -0.29 +- 0.02, Section 3.4)
hosts.sigmaNote: The 0.05 dex for the two hosts is the mean difference between the average of nine strong-line calibrations and the PP04 calibration, which R22 (Section 3.5) propagates as the systematic uncertainty of the strong-line scale; Table 3 prints no per-galaxy error.

rangeNote: The span of the mean [O/H] of the Cepheid samples in R22's Table 3: the SMC (-0.72) to NGC 3147 and NGC 7329 (0.17). A host outside it is an extrapolation of the cited term.

anchorDistances.lmc: 18.477 +- 0.026 mag (Pietrzynski et al. 2019; as R22 adopts it)
